question: In 2022, the Strategic Compass for Security and Defence stated that there would be a reassessment of common costs relating to military missions and operations, with the aim of increasing solidarity and encouraging further involvement in those operations. That reassessment was to be completed by 2023 at the latest. To date, however, there has been no news about the reassessment.

Accordingly: Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy know whether the reassessment has actually been carried out? If it has, is the outcome already available?
answer: The Strategic Compass set the objective that the scope and definition of common costs as well as exercise-related costs would be re-assessed to enhance solidarity and stimulate participation in military missions and operations, also in view of the proposals regarding the EU Rapid Deployment Capacity (RDC).
It also referred to the expansion of the scope of common-costs under the European Peace Facility (EPF) as a means to incentivise force generation for military missions and operations.

Subsequently, a series of workshops with Member States were organised by the European External Action Service (EEAS) in close coordination with the EPF Administrator for operations, as well as informal discussions in relevant Council preparatory bodies, including the Political and Security Committee.

In support of these exchanges, the EEAS, in close coordination with the EPF Administrator for operations, has presented initial proposals for the reassessment of scope of common costs in line with the tasking by the Strategic Compass (notably as regards military missions and operations, EU RDC and military exercises).

Based on these initial proposals and subsequent exchanges of views, amendments on common costs will be included in the High Representative’s formal proposal to amend the EPF Council Decision, with a view to its adoption by the Council later this year.
